newsitem.title: UK: UK Chancellor Clarke at popularity peak - poll.
newsitem.headline: UK Chancellor Clarke at popularity peak - poll.

text.p: British finance minister Kenneth Clarke's popularity has reached a new peak and he is now the most popular Chancellor of the Exchequer since the last general election in 1992, according to an opinion poll.
The MORI poll in Friday's edition of the London Times showed that Clarke, whose popularity plummeted when he raised taxes, is now gaining ground in the runup to this month's annual budget.
In December 1994, his satisfaction rating for voters stood at minus 53 points. That climbed to minus 29 points at the end of last year. The new poll put him at minus four points.
The latest opinion polls show that the ruling Conservatives, who have to call an election by next May, are reducing the huge lead of the opposition Labour Party.
But Prime Minister John Major was dealt a blow on Thursday when official figures showed underlying inflation rose to a three-year high of 3.3 percent in October.
